feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Are teen girls the answer to shortage of public works workers?
entry.summary: Public works jobs across the country are mostly done by men. In Georgia, teenage girls are now trying out those jobs.

entry.title: Who is Jim Jordan, the House Republicans' pick for minority leader?
entry.summary: As House Republicans prepare for life in the minority, they're turning to Jim Jordan as their next leader. In Jordan, they've picked a conservative firebrand and one of Trump's most vocal defenders.

entry.title: The legacy of the 1991 Gulf War and the Americans who carried out the mission
entry.summary: 35 years since the Gulf War ended, veterans reflect on the conflict and its ongoing impact.

entry.title: A cafe in Ukraine relocates from its besieged hometown and reopens
entry.summary: After Russian airstrikes destroyed a popular cafe in a frontline Ukrainian city, the cafe reopened in a safer region, an example of how Ukrainian businesses are trying to survive amid repeated bombing.

entry.title: These voters are looking for change, but don't have high hopes for a divided Congress
entry.summary: North Carolina swing voters are seeking change, but have low expectations that things will actually change.

entry.title: Trisha Paytas comes clean in 'Crying on the Kitchen Floor'
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Trisha Paytas about her memoir, Crying on the Kitchen Floor, and what it's been like to share her life on YouTube since she was 18 years old.

entry.title: A Kennedy relative talks about his family's lawsuit against Trump's 250-foot arch
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Max Kennedy, son of Robert Kennedy Sr., about the Kennedy family's lawsuit to halt the construction of President Trump's 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

entry.title: Trump administration moves forward with converting warehouses into immigration detention
entry.summary: The Trump administration has moved forward with converting 2 massive warehouses into immigration detention centers, despite local outrage and protests.

entry.title: Opponents of Israel's prime minister may have to cross a red line to build new coalition
entry.summary: Opponents of Israel's hardline prime minister are trying to oust him, by building a new coalition. To do so, they may have to cross a red line drawn by most Israeli parties: Work with Arab colleagues.

entry.title: Parts of a historic ghost town face demolition by the National Park Service
entry.summary: Part of a historic town owned by the Park Service is set for demolition as residents oppose the move.
